summary.text: Gerry Pollet is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives from District 46-Position 1 (Seattle area), where he has served since 2011, and he is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
A public interest attorney, he is Executive Director of Heart of America Northwest, a Hanford cleanup advocacy group, and a faculty member at the University of Washington School of Public Health.

paragraphs.text: Gerry Pollet graduated from the University of Washington School of Law in 1983 and chose a career as a public interest attorney working on environmental, consumer and open-government issues.
The House Democrats' biography says he teaches at the University of Washington School of Public Health and at Western Washington University's college of environment and urban planning.
As Executive Director of Heart of America Northwest, he has worked on cleanup of the Hanford Nuclear Reservation.
Pollet took office in the House in 2011.
He serves on the Appropriations, Education, and Postsecondary Education and Workforce Development committees and chairs the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee.
He serves on the board of the Washington Coalition for Open Government.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Pollet said he has been the 46th District's representative since 2012 and described himself as a leader on funding public schools, special education, access to colleges and universities, and the environment.
He said he chairs the committee working to eliminate tax loopholes.
